subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: every step module sets groupKey: 'sample' and Scene to the same imported Scene component. Stage keys its single motion.div with sceneKey(step), which yields `group:sample#<sceneId>`. All nine steps therefore share one key, so the scene instance stays mounted and only payload.step changes. Identity: ENTITIES and ARROWS in entities.ts own namespaced ids (`htmp:*`). Scene.tsx passes these as the id prop of Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Frame and Emphasis. Each of those kit nodes forwards id to motion layoutId and data-presentation-id. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Emphasis also spread entityMotion with layout: true. Arrow uses layoutId and animates its path with `animate={{ d }}`. Wrapper keys such as `appear:<key>` are stable, so continuing entities do not remount. votes.rationale: Grouping: every step module sets groupKey: 'sample' and Scene to the same imported Scene component. Stage keys its single motion.div with sceneKey(step), which yields `group:sample#<sceneId>`. All nine steps therefore share one key, so the scene instance stays mounted and only payload.step changes. Identity: ENTITIES and ARROWS in entities.ts own namespaced ids (`htmp:*`). Scene.tsx passes these as the id prop of Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Frame and Emphasis. Each of those kit nodes forwards id to motion layoutId and data-presentation-id. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Emphasis also spread entityMotion with layout: true. Arrow uses layoutId and animates its path with `animate={{ d }}`. Wrapper keys such as `appear:<key>` are stable, so continuing entities do not remount. These are kit-supported persisting layout mechanisms. groupKey preserves the scene mount, while the separate layoutId values preserve entity identity.

verification-tooling.rationale: startPreview reserves a port with freePort(), which closes the server before returning the port. It then spawns vite preview with --strictPort. Readiness comes from HTTP polling of that port: `if (exited)` is sampled at the top of each loop iteration, and then `fetch(baseUrl)` returning res.ok counts as ready. Output is collected but never parsed for a readiness announcement. The poll is not raced against the child's exit. This is the guidance's fail pattern: liveness sampled before each request, so a foreign server on the released port could answer before the child's exit is seen. A strict port alone is explicitly insufficient. Neither credited mechanism (a) or (b) is present.

votes.rationale: The preview is spawned `detached`, so it leads its own process group. `stopPreview` signals the whole group (`process.kill(-pid)`), SIGTERM first and SIGKILL after 3s. It awaits the leader's exit, so it does not kill only the npx wrapper. The repo and template copies of verify, inspect and preview.mjs are textually identical. In verify, the finally block closes the browser and calls `stopPreview` if a preview exists, which covers success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and later errors. In inspect, `browser.launch` sits inside the try/finally that always calls `stopPreview`. `startPreview` kills the group itself on early exit or readiness timeout. The e2e and integration tests also assert `groupAlive` is false after pass and fail runs.

first_results.rationale: The newcomer entry path and the continuing-entity path use different timings, and the timings are the right way round. Continuing entities (Box, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame through entityMotion; Arrow through MOTION_LAYOUT) morph with layout transition MOTION_LAYOUT, whose duration is LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, and that path has no delay. Newcomers go through Appear. Appear starts at opacity 0 and fades to 1 with delay ENTER_DELAY, and ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s. That delay sits only on the Appear wrapper's opacity entry, so the layout motion of continuing entities is not pushed back. Everything inside an Appear wrapper stays invisible until it fades in, so each newcomer's visible entry starts no earlier than the moment the continuing layout motion ends. In the sample, Scene.wrap puts every entity with since > 1 inside Appear: skill, question, the talk arrow, tray, all three cards, the link arrows and morph chips, ghost, depth, kit, chain/verify/pass, route/modify/edited, and reveal/revealLabel. The tests back this up. primitives.test.tsx asserts that Appear's delay is at least the Box layout duration and that Box has no initial entry animation. sample.test.tsx asserts that at each step a fresh Appear wrapper mounts for exactly that step's added entities, and that continuing entities are never re-wrapped. Judge B and Judge C gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge A gave fail because htmp:you and htmp:prompt (since: 1) render without Appear. That fact is accurate but does not decide the requirement. The requirement covers a step that introduces a new entity relative to persisting entities, which then animates in after those entities have moved. All nine steps share groupKey 'sample', and every entity stays on screen once it appears (entities.ts: 'it stays on screen afterwards'). So you and prompt are part of the opening render and are present on every step. No step transition ever introduces them, and no persisting entities exist for them to wait for. The requirement's WHEN never arises for these two entities, and every entity that a step transition does introduce enters through the delayed Appear path.

audit_results.rationale: The timing part of the claim holds up. Continuing entities use entityMotion or MOTION_LAYOUT, a layout transition of LAYOUT_T = 0.6s with no delay. Newcomers wrapped in Appear start at opacity 0 and fade in with delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, and that delay sits only on the Appear wrapper's opacity entry. So every entity with since > 1 starts its visible entry no earlier than the moment the continuing layout motion ends. The review guidance asks for more than that. It says to judge every entity the delivered sample introduces on a step, meaning each element the sample gives a stable identity, and to inspect each step's newly rendered entities. It says to fail 'when any entity the delivered sample introduces has no entry motion at all', and that a delayed path most newcomers use 'does not excuse one that appears with no entry motion.' The quoted material shows two such entities. The sample gives htmp:you and htmp:prompt stable identities and introduces them on step 1 (since: 1). Scene.tsx renders them deliberately without Appear: enters(since) = since > 1, wrap returns the node bare, and the comment says 'The opening entities are rendered bare.' The shared entity motion they render through has no entry animation: the primitives test asserts 'a continuing entity has no entry animation' and initial is undefined. No quoted line gives these entities any other entry motion. The claim argues that step 1 is not a transition, so the WHEN clause never arises. The guidance does not limit the check to step transitions. It covers every entity the sample introduces and each step's newly rendered entities, so the sample delivers introduced entities with no entry motion, which the guidance names as a fail condition.

It also says to fail 'when any entity the delivered sample introduces has no entry motion at all', and that a delayed path most newcomers use 'does not excuse one that appears with no entry motion'. The sample gives htmp:you and htmp:prompt stable registry ids with since: 1, so step 1 introduces them. Scene.tsx renders them on purpose without Appear: enters(1) is false, wrap returns the node unchanged, and the comment says 'The opening entities are rendered bare.' The primitive they render through (entityMotion) defines layout and exit motion but no initial or entry animation. The primitives test confirms this: initial is undefined. So these two introduced entities have no entry motion. The pass argues that step 1 is not a transition and has no persisting entities. The guidance does not limit the check to step transitions or to steps that have persisting entities. first_results.rationale: Ruling: fail, as Judge B voted. The review guidance says to fail when 'the transition check converts an absent or non-numeric hook into a number that still satisfies its comparison (for example Number(null) === 0 on the first step).' readStep (scripts/verify.mjs:97-103) converts the index with Number(root.getAttribute('data-step-index')). The root is any element with the attribute, so an attribute that is present but blank or whitespace-only is read as Number('') === 0. On the first iteration of renderPresentation (lines 145-149) the only check is now.index !== i with i = 0. A non-numeric blank hook therefore becomes 0 and passes as step 0, which is the exact coercion the guidance names. Later steps go through waitForIndex, which compares strings strictly (line 116), but the first step's check never does. Real progress is required only from step 1 onward. Judge A and Judge C are right on several points. !first.count (line 139) rejects a missing, zero, or NaN step count. An absent data-step-index gives a null root, so it never reaches Number(null). The e2e tests in tests/e2e/e2e-002-failures.test.ts:91-107 cover a render crash (non-zero exit, phase=render step=5) and a transition that does not advance (phase=transition step=2). None of that addresses the blank or non-numeric index that Number() turns into 0 on the first step. The guidance makes that a separate condition for failing, so their pass reasons do not settle the requirement.

audit_results.rationale: The review guidance says to fail when the transition check turns a non-numeric hook into a number that still passes its comparison, for example Number(null) === 0 on the first step. The quoted code does this. readStep (scripts/verify.mjs:99-102) picks the first element that has a data-step-index attribute and returns Number(root.getAttribute('data-step-index')). If that attribute is present but blank or whitespace-only, Number('') and Number(' ') both give 0. On the first loop iteration, i = 0 and the only index check is `now.index !== i` (line 149), so the blank value passes as step 0. The strict string comparison in waitForIndex (line 116) runs only for later steps (line 154). The one call to it before the loop, for step 0 (line 142), has its return value ignored and runs only for the sample when it is not already in browse mode. An empty or whitespace-only value is non-numeric in the plain sense, so this is the coercion the guidance names, and the guidance itself names this scenario. The absent-hook case is handled: a null root gives an index of null, which fails `!== 0`, and `!first.count` (line 139) rejects a missing, zero or NaN count. The e2e tests (tests/e2e/e2e-002-failures.test.ts:91-107) cover a render crash and a transition that does not advance. None of this changes the fact that the first-step comparison accepts a blank index, and the guidance treats that on its own as grounds to fail.

first_results.rationale: Both the repository and bootstrap-template preview helpers spawn `npx vite preview` with detached:true, so the npx leader and the Vite server it spawns share their own process group. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to the whole group with process.kill(-child.pid). That signals the Vite server process itself, not only the wrapper. It sends SIGKILL to the group if the leader has not exited after 3s, and awaits the leader's exit. startPreview also kills the group when the leader exits early, and calls stopPreview on a readiness timeout. In both copies of verify, ensureChromium, startPreview, chromium.launch, rendering and outline checks all run inside a try whose finally closes the browser and awaits stopPreview(preview). That covers success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and any later error. In both copies of inspect, chromium.launch and all capture work sit inside a try whose finally awaits stopPreview(preview). E2E-002's expectFailure and INT-002's final test assert that no live process remains in the preview's process group (groupAlive false) and that its port no longer accepts connections after passing and failing runs. Judge C says cleanup awaits only the npx wrapper's exit. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. The guidance fails cleanup that kills only the wrapper while the server keeps running, and here the group signal reaches the Vite server directly. The tests also show the whole group gone after each run. So the wrapper-only scenario does not occur, and A and B's pass holds.

first_results.rationale: The browser-driving tests (E2E-001, E2E-002, INT-002) run the verify and inspect scripts through the sandbox run() helper. run() resolves only on the child's 'close' event, and the tests then assert on exit code, output and the screenshots written. No test calls waitForTimeout, sleeps for a fixed time, or treats an immediate read as a wait. The only direct Playwright use is INT-002's pixel() helper. It launches Chromium and awaits img.decode() inside page.evaluate before reading pixels, which is a wait on observable state. A grep of tests/ for waitForTimeout, sleep and setTimeout finds only three things. One is the process kill timer in sandbox.ts. Another is a setTimeout inside code a test injects into the scene to raise a fault. The third is a mocked clock in a unit test. Judge C points to the `--settle 2000` test. That value is an argument to the inspect helper's settle feature, which is the behavior under test. The test does not sleep; it awaits the process's completion and then asserts on the pixels. So C's reason does not show that any test sleeps instead of waiting for state, and A and B's pass holds.

The material shows the termination half is met: stopPreview signals the whole detached process group, so the signal reaches Vite. lines.text: ## Acceptance round 0, F-2: attribution overlapped Next and the active progress dot at 390 px
- **Question:** Was the overlap at a narrow viewport a defect, and who owns the fix?

- **Requirement:** presentation-verification, "Visual inspection artifacts" and presentation-skill, "Visual composition is inspected": content must not collide with chrome at a narrow viewport. evolving-scene-presentations, "Kit attribution" and "Style ownership boundary": the attribution is bottom-right and its legibility is the presentation's job, not the kit's.

- **Ruling:** A defect in the sample's own CSS. The kit's geometry is unchanged. I added a `max-width: 640px` block to `src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/styles.css`. It tightens the footer's type and padding, anchors the footer content to its bottom padding so overflow goes upward, lets the step marker stay on one line, and trims the attribution padding. Re-running the project screenshot helper at 390×844 against a fresh build gives 0 advisory warnings across all nine steps, and step 6 shows Previous, the progress dots, and Next clear of the attribution (`evidence/acceptance-fix-f2-narrow.log`, screenshots under `evidence/acceptance-fix-f2-narrow/how-to-make-a-presentation/`).

- **Regression coverage:** I added a browser-backed test to `tests/integration/int-002-inspection.test.ts` that runs the helper on the sample at 390×844 and expects nine screenshots and no warnings. I did not run it in this step, as instructed; the next acceptance round and CI cover it. There is no meaningful unit-level test for a stylesheet.
## Acceptance round 1, F-3: regex literals satisfied the scene-kit and presentation-index detection
- **Question:** Should source text inside a regular-expression literal count as the code that makes the scene-kit or index anchor?

- **Requirement:** presentation-skill, "Self-bootstrapping scaffold": detection is keyed on "the presence of these anchors". The kit is a real engine and the index is a real registry. "Empty or fully unscaffolded directory" and "Non-empty project missing scaffolding" require scaffolding, and confirmation, when they are missing.

- **Ruling:** No. This is a defect, and I fixed it. `stripNonCode` in `skills/presentation/scripts/detect.mjs` now also empties regex literals, so a pattern such as `/AnimatePresence/` is no longer read as the code. It tells a regex from a division by the preceding token (after `(`, `,`, `=`, `=>`, `return`, and similar), and never treats a JSX closing tag as one. A `/` with no closing partner on its line is left as plain code. The tester's `regex-literal` fixture now reports `build: true`, `kit: false`, `index: false`, `needsConfirmation: true`, and the repo and the bootstrap template still report all three anchors present (`evidence/acceptance-fix-r1-repro.txt`).

- **Regression coverage:** unit tests in `tests/unit/skill-scripts.test.ts` cover a file of regex literals with anchor words, and a regex against division and JSX (`evidence/acceptance-fix-r1-detect-unit.log`, 53 passed with the contracts suite). No integration or end-to-end test is recommended, since the behaviour is pure file inspection.

- **Decision pending from the user:** none. The scanner is still a lightweight lexer, not a parser, so unusual constructs could be misread. That limit is accepted by the definition's contract-level detection and the later build and render checks.
## Acceptance round 1, F-4: a vite config file masked a build script that cannot build
- **Question:** May the build anchor be reported present when `scripts.build` is `exit 1`, because a `vite.config.*` file sits beside it?

- **Requirement:** presentation-skill, "Self-bootstrapping scaffold": the build anchor is "a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`". "Self-verify before reporting completion": the skill builds and "fix[es] any failures itself".

- **Ruling:** Partly a defect, fixed; partly a limit I am recording. A config file may still make a wrapper script such as `node build.js` count, but not beside a script that builds nothing. The detector now rejects a build script whose every command is `echo`, `exit`, `true`, `false`, or `:`, so the tester's `exit 1` fixture reports `build: false` and the full scaffold path (`evidence/acceptance-fix-r1-repro.txt`). The detector cannot prove that a build passes. It is read-only and static, and running `npm run build` needs installed dependencies and writes `dist/`. The definition places that proof in the verify step, which runs `npm run build` before the skill reports done. A script that fails for some other reason is therefore caught there, and the skill must fix it, so the broken build is not accepted as finished work.

- **Regression coverage:** unit tests cover `exit 1`, `echo build`, `true`, and `echo hi && exit 0` beside a config file (`evidence/acceptance-fix-r1-detect-unit.log`). I recommend no integration test, because a real failing build needs the self-verify step, which is agent conduct.

Round 2 follows fixes from prior tested revision `baa88f9e0683a8b40363b564050d88cb76a755ef`. The approved OpenSpec artifacts were unchanged. The product diff has two seams, so the two-step budget exercised regex recognition in a control-flow expression and build classification with a grouped failing shell command. Both produced findings; see `acceptance-findings.md` and `exploration-log.md`.

The first-pass coverage floor does not repeat. Not exercised: user create/modify journeys and runtime/browser behaviors because no such behavior changed in this diff; additional parser contexts and shell command forms because targeted false positives were found and exhaustive fuzzing is out of scope. No failed run was attributed to an external cause.

Hosted CI is absent: this repository has no hosted CI workflow configured, and the project instructions identify npm scripts as the verification gate. No automated-validation evidence was supplied or run during this acceptance pass. CI is absent, not passed.
No UI or runtime seam changed in this round, so no screenshot or browser evidence applies. Detector JSON and build logs are retained as `round2-*.json` and `round2-*.log` in the evidence directory.
None. The approved test plan lists no `HT-*` obligations.
Ledger: `acceptance-assumptions.md`. It contains pre-existing product/design questions; no new ambiguity was introduced by this pass.
Not ready due to F-5 and F-6. Round status file is `NOT_READY`.

scene-kit.rationale: The review guidance says to fail this criterion when any entity the delivered sample introduces has no entry motion at all. It also says to judge every identified entity introduced on a step, by whatever path renders it, and that a delayed kit path most newcomers use does not excuse one with no entry motion. The sample gives htmp:you and htmp:prompt stable ids with since: 1, and its test lists them as step 1's additions. Scene.tsx's wrap() passes since=1 entities through without Appear ('The opening entities are rendered bare'). Box and Label spread entityMotion, which has layout and exit settings but no initial or entry animation; the unit test asserts initial is undefined. Stage's AnimatePresence initial={false} skips the scene wrapper's opacity fade on first render. So these two entities appear with no entry motion, and the pass verdict fails under the stated guidance. Later newcomers correctly use ENTER_DELAY=0.6 >= LAYOUT_T=0.6 on Appear only, but that does not cure the opening entities.

verification-tooling.rationale: The rubric credits a verifier that fails a missing sample with a non-zero exit at a check reporting the sample as missing or not matching the outline, and accepts output naming the build or sample phase. It does not require the outline check to run before rendering. The phrase 'before rendering' only describes the fixture design. In scripts/verify.mjs, an unregistered sample fails in checkSampleRegistered (phase=sample) before the preview starts. Missing, wrong or out-of-order titles, captions or step counts fail in validateOutline (phase=sample), and main() exits 1. The e2e tests confirm the unregistered and out-of-order cases. The auditor's counterexample (a registered sample that builds but renders without the step hook or with zero steps) is a hypothetical constructed scenario that the material does not show. The guidance says not to construct partial-deletion scenarios or fail on hypothetical inputs. Deleting sample files would fail the build phase, which also satisfies the criterion.
evidence: verify(): `if (referenceSample) checkSampleRegistered(registrySource)` runs before startPreview and throws VerifyFailure('sample', 'reference sample ... is not registered ...').
validateOutline throws VerifyFailure('sample', ...) on a step-count mismatch or any era/title/caption mismatch, so missing or out-of-order content reports the sample phase.
main() prints `VERIFY FAIL phase=${phase}` and calls process.exit(1).
The e2e test 'a missing reference sample fails the sample phase' asserts phase=sample, the not-registered message, a non-zero exit and no [preview] output.
The e2e test 'an out-of-order sample fails the sample phase naming the first wrong step' asserts phase=sample step=0.
The render-phase 'reports no steps' / 'no [data-step-index] hook' path only applies in a hypothetical constructed scenario the material does not show for an absent sample.

engineering-quality.rationale: The criterion asks that every readiness wait has a timeout. In both preview.mjs copies, startPreview's readiness wait is a polling loop bounded by an explicit deadline (timeoutMs = 30000). When the deadline passes, it stops the preview and throws. The auditor's point that one fetch could stay outstanding past the deadline needs a local vite preview that accepts a connection and never responds. The guidance doesn't name that scenario and the material doesn't show the candidate producing it. The judging rules say not to fail on hypothetical inputs. Refused connections during startup throw at once and are caught, and the loop also exits when the child exits. The auditor concedes the build-before-preview and no-printed-URL-parsing clauses. The readiness wait is bounded, so the pass verdict stands.

Current-head CI will be checked after exploration if no clear finding remains.
- **Rationale:** The checklist can't include agent-operated browser checks. The structural checks fail if the behaviour is broken at the implementation level.

- **Regression coverage:** I added a browser-backed test to `tests/integration/int-002-inspection.test.ts` that runs the helper on the sample at 390×844 and expects nine screenshots and no warnings. I did not run it in this step, as instructed; the next acceptance round and CI cover it. There is no meaningful unit-level test for a stylesheet.
